title: Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: remaining charge — special grace prepared for some only makes baptism useless for the rest; we deny the consequence
pass_a_gloss: That therefore alone remains, that because we say that special grace, and in fact leading unto glory, is prepared and given unto certain ones of the mere good pleasure of God, unto others neither prepared nor given, therefore we should be judged to establish Baptism as altogether useless as to these latter. We deny this consequence.
pass_b_english: So only this remains: because we say special grace that in fact leads to glory is prepared and given to some of God's mere good pleasure, and to others neither prepared nor given, we are judged to make baptism altogether useless for these latter. We deny that consequence.
source_text: Illud igitur unum reliquum est, ut quia nos dicimus specialem gratiam, et de facto ad gloriam perducentem quibusdam ex mero Dei beneplacito praeparari et donari, aliis nec praeparari nec donari, idcirco judicemur statuere Baptismum quoad hosce posteriores prorsus inutilem. Nos negamus hanc consequentiam.
